CI's mutant lines refer to the head CI ran; once a commit moves code, find each mutant by its function and replacement.

Otherwise apply the exemption rule and written reason of the workflow doc or the testing doc it names (`exempted: <reason>`); with no such rule, remove it. CI fails until one lands; never report it as equivalent alone.
- Run only the gate and the tests your findings name. Suites the workflow doc gives to CI, such as mutation testing (`cargo mutants`), benchmarks and backstops, run in CI: read their result from the CI log, and report when you need one reproduced.
- Run every command in the foreground, so it ends before your turn does; start no background or detached process. When the gate outlasts one tool call, run the narrowest test set your change reaches in the foreground and leave the full gate to the job-end gate. The project's workflow doc is $HOME/work/fiber-worktrees/cli/2863-feedback-diagnostics/docs/workflow.md; it wins where it speaks.

## Findings

VERDICT standards: CHANGES
P2 crates/contract/src/feedback.rs:14 — The feedback seam passes a session identifier as `Option<&str>`, and the TUI strips `SessionId` to a string before calling it. This breaks the rule that each kind of identifier has its own newtype (`docs/code-quality.md`, “Types”). Keep `SessionId` typed across the seam and diagnostics APIs.
P2 crates/main/src/main.rs:662 — `feedback_session` implements feedback-specific session selection and delegate validation in `main`, contrary to its composition-root rule: “No feature logic” (`docs/architecture.md`, module table). Move this behavior into `cli`; let `main` dispatch it.

VERDICT spec: CHANGES
P1 crates/cli/src/feedback.rs:219 — `entry()` accepts a `debug` line without checking that `data` is an object, then copies the raw JSON line into the report. An invalid line can therefore carry arbitrary content into the attachment, contrary to the plan’s rule that a debug line has “`data`, an object of named values” and that uncertain lines are omitted — validate the debug field shape before copying the line.

VERDICT overbuild: CHANGES

A finding that names a pattern a test relies on (a real-clock hold, a `sleep`, a fixed wait) is a class: search the PR's diff for that pattern and remove it from every test the PR adds or changes. The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. ## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

An additive edit to an existing file outside it (a new enum variant, match arm, struct field, `mod` line, slash-table entry, test function or docs section) is allowed: add lines only, delete none, and list each such file in your report; the second PR to merge takes main and resolves. Before pushing, check the branch's whole diff against it: `git diff --name-only --no-renames origin/main...HEAD`, which lists a renamed file under its old path as well. A file outside Files must already exist on main and show zero deleted lines in `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD -- <path>`.
- Before the first task, check the plan against b9f8b8ba8cb3249078e656b1e60260c4f43d8b2d, which may be newer than the plan: every path it names that the plan does not create exists (`git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>`), and `git grep -n` finds every existing function, type, constant and test it names, tests in every crate or package included. A miss means main moved under the plan: stop and report each miss with what main has in its place.
- Every acceptance criterion and doc requirement the ticket names ships. When one can't, stop and report it as a design question.
- Stop and report before you add or change a public interface the plan's Interfaces don't list, delete or weaken a test or doc sentence you did not add, loosen any test's timeout, wait, retry count or numeric tolerance (your own tests included) that neither the plan nor the ticket's acceptance criteria call for, or add a dependency. For a looser bound, report the cause it would hide.
- When the code makes a plan ruling wrong or unworkable, stop and report it with the evidence; build no alternative.
- Run the tasks in order, each test first, and pass each task's gate and commit before starting the next.
- Run only the gate and the tests your tasks name. Suites the workflow doc gives to CI, such as mutation testing (`cargo mutants`), benchmarks and backstops, run in CI: read their result from the CI log, and report when you need one reproduced.
- Run every command in the foreground, so it ends before your turn does; start no background or detached process. When the gate outlasts one tool call, run the narrowest test set your change reaches in the foreground and leave the full gate to the job-end gate. The pi harness turns a command still running after 30s into a job it manages, which is not a detached process: wait on it with the `jobs` tool, `action: "wait"`, its id and `timeout: 3600`, and repeat until it ends. Don't poll its log; bare `sleep` is blocked.
- A look or probe task (running the program or a TUI to see what it does) gets 3 probe rounds. Then end with `STATUS: NEEDS_CONTEXT` and a verdict digest: what each round showed and what stays unknown.
- Run every command in your worktree, each one starting `cd $HOME/work/fiber-worktrees/cli/2863-feedback-diagnostics &&`: a shell's working directory can reset between calls, and a build or test run elsewhere lands in another agent's checkout. Read main's version of a file with `git show origin/main:<path>`.
- Write shell commands that run on both macOS (BSD tools) and Linux (GNU): edit a file with the edit tool or `perl -pi -e`, since `sed -i` takes different arguments on each.
- Commit each new script under `bin/` as executable: `chmod 755` it, then `git ls-files -s <path>` shows mode `100755`.
- Mark a deliberate shortcut with a `debt: <ceiling>, <upgrade trigger>` comment. A shortcut that would weaken a rule a doc, spec or ticket states gets no marker: stop and report.
- Commit your work before any command that discards changes (`git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore`, a rebase). Make a scratch commit, such as one kept as evidence, on a throwaway branch (`git switch -c scratch/<name>`), then switch back to the lane branch and delete the scratch one.
- Give each new comparison, match guard and `&&`/`||` condition a test that fails when it flips: for a comparison, values at, just below and just above the edge. See each new assert fail against deliberately broken code before you rely on it.
- A test asserts behaviour: pin a fixture by a tag or by the repo it builds, never by a commit sha, which a rebase rewrites.
- Give each blocking wait in a test you add (a join, a `recv`, an attempt-count loop) a deadline, so a bug fails the test instead of hanging it.
- Write comments that state the rule itself, never "ruling N" or "per the plan".
- When the plan names a Red commit, make it the branch's first commit, holding only those files.
- To rebuild the branch's history, reset to the merge-base (`git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)`), never to `origin/main` and never with `git checkout <branch> -- .`: both drop main's newer changes.
- Set work aside with a commit. To compare against main, build main in a throwaway worktree (`git worktree add --detach ../cmp-<branch> origin/main`, then `git worktree remove` it). Only a worktree or branch you created is yours to remove: the shared checkout is never a target of `git worktree remove` or `git branch -D`, and `ship-pr` cleans up your own worktree when you run it from outside that worktree. The stash stack is shared with every other worktree of the repo, so `git stash` can pop another agent's changes.
- Before each commit, run the formatter the gate checks with (e.g. `cargo fmt` for `cargo fmt --check`), so no commit holds an unformatted file, then the gate passes before the push: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo fmt --check -p cli && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p cli --all-targets -- -D warnings && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p cli && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo fmt --check -p contract && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p contract --all-targets -- -D warnings && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p contract && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo fmt --check -p main && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p main --bins --tests -- -D warnings && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p main --bins --tests && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo fmt --check -p tui && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p tui --all-targets -- -D warnings && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p tui && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask signal-sites && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask compiled-in && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask image-isolation && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask tui-isolation && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask dependency-list && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 bash scripts/check && bash scripts/check-docs`. Run each of its commands on its own with output redirected to a file, and read its exit code before the next; a pipe hides the exit code.
- Refer to other issues as `see #N` or `#N's case` in commit messages and PR text. GitHub closes any issue a closing keyword (close, fix, resolve and their forms) precedes, so the only issue reference you write with one is the PR body's closing line.
- Push the branch. When no PR is open on it, open a draft PR whose title says what the change does, with no issue number (the squash merge appends the PR's own), and whose body starts with `Resolves #2863`. The body holds every line the workflow doc requires in a PR body, the line `Co-authored with Claude Code.`, and an `Implemented by: <model id>` line (the id from your `Model:` report line), and names only the checks that ran and passed, each with its command. Then end the job: whoever started you reads the mutant list once the job that lists it finishes, and waits on the rest of CI.

## Report

First line: `Model: <the id your runtime reports, or unknown>`. Then the PR URL and its head SHA with the gate's last output line quoted from its log (report a pass only beside a log that ends in one), or a failure triage (the step, the command, its output tail), nothing in between. Then **Friction**: up to 3 bullets on what slowed you, what the plan or docs got wrong or left out, and what you would change ("none" is fine). End with a STATUS line.
Time-dependent behaviour is tested under an injected clock; no test reads or sleeps on the real clock, and a test advances a fake clock only after a signal that the code under test is waiting on it (docs/testing.md "Waits and timeouts").
--label mutants



---

Give each shell command that builds or runs tests a timeout of at least 600 seconds; a shorter limit kills the run partway and reads as a failure.
End your final message with a single trailing line that is exactly one of: STATUS: DONE, STATUS: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, STATUS: BLOCKED, STATUS: NEEDS_CONTEXT, or STATUS: ERROR. When you need an answer from the orchestrator before you can proceed, put your question in the message body and end with STATUS: NEEDS_CONTEXT.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. ## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. ## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.
''')

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. ## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.
''')

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;

It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.
''')

It carries no session content: no messages, tool calls or output. When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

When you cannot sign in to GitHub, the printed link still carries the whole report except its diagnostics; when the report is too long for a link, the command says to attach the file instead.

## What the report holds

The version and platform, how Fiber was installed, the description, the `fiber doctor` output verbatim, and a Diagnostics section. What each part means is [Commands and flags](../invocation.md#commands-and-flags).

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics section helps with a problem in one session. It holds:

- the session's id, and the command that exports its log, `fiber sessions export <id>`. The export holds your prompts and the model's replies, so send it privately to whoever asked, never in an issue;
- the session's diagnostic log lines, which record failures and timings and never your prompts, the model's text, a tool's arguments, a credential or a setting's value. An extension's own `extension_log` lines are left out, because Fiber cannot vouch for what an extension wrote;
- the hub's lines from the last day, and any older hub line that names the session;
- each crash report for the session, with the thread, the source location and the backtrace, and without the panic message.

`fiber feedback` uses the newest session in the current project. Name another session, from any project, with `--session <id>`; an id that names no session, or a delegate, fails with `session_not_found` and writes no report. With no session, the section holds the hub's lines only. In the terminal, `/feedback` uses the session on screen; a session on another machine's hub has no diagnostic lines here, and the report says so.

The report holds at most the newest 500 hub lines and 2,000 session lines. Errors and warnings are kept first, and the report says how many earlier session lines it left out. Both limits were chosen, not measured ([Fiber home](../state.md#what-each-part-holds)). Anything Fiber is unsure of is left out. The Diagnostics section is in the saved file only, not in the issue link, so read the file before you attach it.

edits.newText:
#   - every build-cache entry (key v0-rust-...) that a newer generation of the
#     same cache replaced: entries sharing a ref and a key up to its last
#     two dashes, all but those whose lock hash (last segment) equals the
#     newest entry's;

| ([.[] | select(.key | startswith("v0-rust-"))]
        | group_by([.ref, (.key | sub("-[^-]*-[^-]*$"; ""))])
        | map(sort_by(.created_at) | reverse | (.[0].key | sub(".*-"; "")) as $lock
            | map(select((.key | sub(".*-"; "")) != $lock)) | .[])) as $old

        | group_by([.ref, (.key | sub("-[^-]*$"; ""))])
        | map(sort_by(.created_at) | reverse | .[1:][])) as $old

cd $HOME/work/fiber-worktrees/ci/2984-cache-prune-generations && gh pr create --draft --title "Prune superseded Actions cache generations by lock hash" --body "Resolves #2984

Root cause: \`doomed\` in \`scripts/cache-prune\` grouped build-cache entries by \`[.ref, (.key | sub(\"-[^-]*\$\"; \"\"))]\`. rust-cache keys end in \`-<env hash>-<lock hash>\`, so dropping one segment leaves the env hash in the group key; a new lock generation usually changes the env hash too, so each generation falls in a group of its own and \`.[1:]\` deletes nothing. The fix groups by the key minus its last two dash segments and deletes every entry whose lock hash (last segment) differs from the newest entry's, keeping every entry on the current lock (including distinct env hashes).

Evidence the fix holds:
- New fixture test \`build_generations_delete_the_superseded_lock\` fails on the base (deletes nothing, \`left: []\`) and passes after the fix; the existing \`build_generations_keep_only_the_newest_of_each_group\` passes unchanged before and after.
- Live read-only dry-run names exactly the five dead 06b9f28a ids from the ticket and no current-lock entry (output below).
- \`docs/ci.md\` already states the intended behaviour; left as is per acceptance. No \`permissions:\` change. The 9.5 GB threshold stays (unthresholded delete kept).

Live dry-run (\`GITHUB_REPOSITORY=aakshintala/fiber bash scripts/cache-prune --dry-run\`, read-only):

\`\`\`
cache size before: 10400683547 bytes
would delete cache 9254311112
would delete cache 9254702211
would delete cache 9256531922
would delete cache 9254990675
would delete cache 9254229731
cache size after: 10400683547 bytes
\`\`\`

Those five ids are the ticket's dead 06b9f28a generation (b771e0df, f011ef13, b558bb6d, 077ade60, 7e9f1f9d); none of the current-lock 2681f625 entries is named, including both x64 env hashes 7543b454 and a74c6f26.

Doc friction: none

Checks that ran and passed:
- \`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p xtask --test cache_prune\` — 11 passed
- \`shellcheck --shell=bash scripts/cache-prune\` — clean
- \`cargo fmt --check -p xtask\` — clean
- \`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p loop --test handoff --test inner_calls --test invariants\` — 109 passed
- \`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p main --test delegates delegate_ask_user_reaches_parent_through_wake_and_answers_resume_it --test release_pack install_sh_serves_the_target_and_refuses_a_mismatch\` — 2 passed

Note: a local full \`scripts/check\` run failed on 12 tests in untouched crates (loop handoff/inner_calls/invariants, main delegates/release_pack), all on real-time waits under heavy machine load (load average ~30, 21 users); every one passes outside the full-suite run. The full gate is left for CI on a clean machine.

Co-authored with Claude Code.

Root cause: \`doomed\` in \`scripts/cache-prune\` grouped build-cache entries by \`[.ref, (.key | sub(\"-[^-]*\$\"; \"\"))]\`. rust-cache keys end in \`-<env hash>-<lock hash>\`, so dropping one segment leaves the env hash in the group key; a new lock generation usually changes the env hash too, so each generation falls in a group of its own and \`.[1:]\` deletes nothing. The fix groups by the key minus its last two dash segments and deletes every entry whose lock hash (last segment) differs from the newest entry's, keeping every entry on the current lock (including distinct env hashes).

- New fixture test \`build_generations_delete_the_superseded_lock\` fails on the base (deletes nothing, \`left: []\`) and passes after the fix; the existing \`build_generations_keep_only_the_newest_of_each_group\` passes unchanged before and after.
